chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who wears a turban and does not let one end hang in front and the other at the back, so an illness strikes him and there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself.

key_terms.يَتَحَنَّكْ: To arrange the turban with ends hanging front and back

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical consequence of improperly wearing a turban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical act of wearing a turban with the ritual of *tahannuk* (arranging the ends), warning that neglecting this specific Sunnah invites a unique, incurable ailment. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and physical consequences of adhering to prophetic customs, framing the *tahannuk* not merely as etiquette but as a source of divine protection and health.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who wears a turban and does not Tahannak it (lets one end hang in front and the other at the back), so an illness strikes him and there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One who wears a turban without tahannak (allowing one end to hang down on one’s front side and the other end down one’s back side), if he faces an illness without cure he then must not blame anyone for it except his own-self.’”
